title: Local fixed ideal and rational jets for a split torus action
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $T=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-gm-ga], and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with an algebraic $T$-action (a morphism $T\times_kX\to X$ satisfying associativity and identity, with product [def-pc-fibre-product]). Suppose a closed subscheme $F\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] represents the subfunctor of points fixed after every commutative algebra extension. Let $x\in F(k)$, put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal; the residue field is $k$. For $t\in T(k)$ let $t^*$ be the induced $k$-algebra automorphism of $A$. Set $J=(t^*f-f\mid t\in T(k),\ f\in\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The closed immersion induces an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{F,x}\cong A/J$ of local $k$-algebras. For every $n\geq1$, $A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ is a finite-dimensional rational $T$-algebra: its coaction into $(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\otimes_k k[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ is a $k$-algebra map satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity, and its evaluation at $t$ is induced by $t^*$. The ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ is a rational subrepresentation, the quotient $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ has its induced coaction, and the natural surjection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is $T$-equivariant. A rational representation here means a $k$-vector space with a linear coaction satisfying these two identities; no regularity or smoothness of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 13.4, printed p.255 (difference ideal); proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256 (rational finite jets), applied to the split torus and its schematically dense rational points. The affine coefficient interpretation identifies the scheme-theoretic fixed ideal, without assuming that the fixed scheme is reduced.

proof.text: Put $C=k[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, viewed as the ring of finite sums in exponents $\mathbf Z^r$. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the coordinate description [def-sc-gm-ga] identifies $k[T]=C$. For every $k$-algebra $D$, the mutually inverse maps $D\otimes_k C\leftrightarrow D[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ send $d\otimes z^u$ to the monomial with coefficient $d$, and $\sum d_uz^u$ to $\sum d_u\otimes z^u$; bilinearity and the finite-sum multiplication check both composites and the algebra structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Pullback of the action is therefore a $k$-algebra map $c:B\to B\otimes_kC$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Pulling back the given associativity and identity diagrams gives $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)c=1$, where $\Delta(z_i)=z_i\otimes z_i$ and $\epsilon(z_i)=1$. The symmetry of tensor factors is understood. Evaluation of $c(b)$ at $t$ is the pullback $t^*b$, directly by composing the action with $(t,1_X)$.

source.place: Chapter 1(f), printed p.26, action diagrams; Chapter 13, Lemma 13.4, printed p.255: affine coordinate preparation.

proof.text: Write $d_b=c(b)-b\otimes1=\sum_u a_{b,u}z^u$, and let $I\subset B$ be generated by all $a_{b,u}$. A $k$-algebra map $q:B\to R$ kills $I$ exactly when $(q\otimes1)c(b)=q(b)\otimes1$ for every $b$, by uniqueness of the Laurent coefficients. This is exactly the assertion that the point $q$ is fixed after every $R$-algebra extension: that identity can be evaluated at every $t\in T(R')$ after any $R\to R'$. Conversely take $R'=R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ and its universal torus point $(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ to recover the identity. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ represents the specified fixed subfunctor, scheme-theoretically. Indeed [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes the given $F$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(B/K)$; the quotient maps to $B/I$ and $B/K$ and equality of the represented subfunctors imply $K\subseteq I$ and $I\subseteq K$, respectively. Thus $K=I$. This uses algebra-valued points, and never passes to a radical ideal.

source.place: Lemma 13.4, printed p.255, factorization through the difference ideal; coefficient expansion makes the all-extension fixed functor explicit.

proof.text: The field $k$ is infinite: if it were finite, the nonconstant polynomial $\prod_{a\in k}(U-a)-1$ would have no root, contrary to algebraic closedness. Let $I_0=(t^*b-b\mid t\in T(k),\ b\in B)$. Every such difference is an evaluation of $d_b$, so $I_0\subseteq I$. Regard $I_0$ as a $k$-linear subspace of $B$. All evaluations of each $d_b$ lie in $I_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-laurent-vector-evaluation-test] with $V=B$, $W=I_0$ to obtain $a_{b,u}\in I_0$ for every $b,u$. Consequently $I=I_0$. The coefficient lemma applies to the possibly infinite-dimensional vector space $B$, so no unjustified finite-dimensionality or reducedness assumption enters here.

source.place: Lemma 13.4, printed p.255, and Remark 1.14, printed p.10: rational-point differences recover all coefficient equations.

proof.text:
Let $x:B\to k$ be the given rational point and $\mathfrak p=\ker x$. Since $x$ is fixed, $x(t^*b)=x(b)$, so $I_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $t^*\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p$ (use $t^{-1}$ for the reverse inclusion). Identify $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ and its stalk maps by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization]. The fraction description gives $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p A$ and $t^*(b/s)=t^*b/t^*s$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Each generator $t^*b-b$ of $I_0$ is the difference of $b-x(b)\in\mathfrak p$, so $I_0A\subseteq J$. Conversely, for $b/s\in\mathfrak m$ (indeed for any fraction) one has
$$t^*(b/s)-b/s=\frac{s(t^*b-b)-b(t^*s-s)}{s\,t^*s}\in I_0A.$$
Both denominators avoid $\mathfrak p$. Thus $J=I_0A=IA$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], applied to $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, identifies the stalk of $F=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ at $x$ with $A/IA=A/J$, with exactly the map induced by the closed immersion.

source.place: Lemma 13.4 and its proof, printed p.255; explicit localization calculation extending the argument to arbitrary affine finite-type schemes.

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq1$ and put $N=n+1$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_e$ of $B$, and set $y_i=b_i-x(b_i)$. These generate $\mathfrak p$: expand any polynomial in the $b_i$ around the scalars $x(b_i)$; its constant term is its value at $x$, and all other terms are divisible by some $y_i$. The quotient $D_N=B/\mathfrak p^N$ is spanned over $k$ by the finitely many monomials $y_1^{a_1}\cdots y_e^{a_e}$ of total degree $<N$. Every $s\notin\mathfrak p$ has image $x(s)+v$, with $x(s)\ne0$ and $v^N=0$ in $D_N$, and has inverse
$$x(s)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-v/x(s))^j.$$
The fraction universal property [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] therefore extends $B\to D_N$ to $A\to D_N$. Its kernel contains $\mathfrak m^N$, and the resulting map $A/\mathfrak m^N\to D_N$ is inverse to $D_N\to A/\mathfrak m^N$: one composite fixes $B$, the other fixes every fraction $b/s$, since both send $s^{-1}$ to the unique inverse of $s$. This proves the canonical algebra isomorphism and finite-dimensionality, also when $e=0$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, finite jet spaces; the affine quotient and finite spanning monomials spell out the local-algebra input.

proof.text: Fixedness of $x$ on all algebra-valued points says $(x\otimes1)c(b)=x(b)1_C$; in Laurent coefficients this says that $c(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak p[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$. Multiplicativity then gives $c(\mathfrak p^N)\subseteq\mathfrak p^N[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$. Reducing all coefficients modulo $\mathfrak p^N$ defines a $k$-algebra coaction $c_N:D_N\to D_N\otimes_k C$. Coassociativity and the counit identity descend by applying coefficient reduction to those of $c$; coefficient reduction in one or two sets of Laurent variables commutes with substitution $z_i\mapsto z_iw_i$ and $z_i\mapsto1$. Transport $c_N$ along the explicit isomorphism of step 5 to $A/\mathfrak m^N$. Its evaluation at $t$ agrees on $B$ with $t^*$ by step 1, and therefore on all fractions by uniqueness of inverses. The same calculation with $\mathfrak p$ shows that $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^N$ is a subcomodule. Reduction $D_N\to D_2$ commutes coefficientwise with $c_N,c_2$ and sends $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^N$ onto $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$. Under the fraction identifications this is exactly the required surjective equivariant map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. For $n=1$ it is the identity. These are rational representations in the coaction sense specified in the statement.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, rational jet representations and the cotangent quotient; explicit coaction descent.
